## Data Source

The data comes from the [Palmer Penguins dataset](https://allisonhorst.github.io/palmerpenguins/), collected and made available by Dr. Kristen Gorman and the Palmer Station Long Term Ecological Research (LTER) Program. The data is available under a [CC0 license](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/).

```{python}
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from palmerpenguins import load_penguins
```

## Data Cleaning

Clean the data before doing analysis

```{python}
penguins = load_penguins()

penguins_clean = penguins.dropna(subset=["species", "body_mass_g"])

penguins_clean.head()
```

## Species Calculation 

Calculate the body mass for each species

```{python}
penguins_clean.groupby("species")["body_mass_g"].mean()
```

## Figure of Body mass by species

Apply the figure to show the comparison of body mass from different species

```{python}
#| label: fig-penguin-mass-python
#| fig-cap: "Body mass of penguins by species."

penguins_clean.boxplot(column="body_mass_g", by="species")
plt.xlabel("Species")
plt.ylabel("Body mass (g)")
plt.suptitle("")
plt.title("")
plt.show()
```

The fgiure shows the body mass distribution of three penguin species. From the figure, we can see that Adelie and Chinstrap have similar range of body masses, while Gentoo has a much higher overall distribution than the former two species.
